title: Foundation Underpinning vs Seismic Retrofit: What Your Bay Area Home Actually Needs
metaTitle: Underpinning vs Seismic Retrofit: Which Does Your SF Home Need?
excerpt: Underpinning fixes settling. Seismic retrofit prepares for earthquakes. They're different problems with different price tags — and most Bay Area homes need one or the other, not both. Here's how to tell which.
proposalRationale: The concrete-foundations service page is ranking (106 impressions, pos 8.4, 1 click). Existing content covers underpinning cost and 5 signs of foundation trouble but nothing on seismic retrofit — a huge cluster gap given SF's mandatory soft-story ordinance and the Earthquake Brace + Bolt program ($3K grant). This post disambiguates two commonly confused services, targets high-intent commercial queries, and strengthens the foundation cluster. Also supports future retrofit ad group activation. Direct answer content perfect for AI Overview citation.

outline.h2: The Short Answer: Different Problems, Different Fixes
outline.notes: Underpinning: your foundation is failing (settling, cracking) and needs structural reinforcement below grade. Cost $15K-$50K+. Seismic retrofit: your foundation is fine but the connection to the framing above isn't earthquake-ready. Cost $3K-$15K for a typical bolt+brace, $60K-$200K+ for soft-story retrofit. Most SF homes need one, not both.

outline.h2: How to Tell Which Your Home Needs
outline.notes: Diagnostic framework: floors sloping / diagonal cracks / doors sticking = underpinning territory. Pre-1980 wood frame on cripple wall = seismic retrofit territory. Marina fill 1920s-1940s = probably both. First step: crawlspace inspection.

outline.h2: Foundation Underpinning: When Settling Is the Problem
outline.notes: Cross-link to existing underpinning cost post. Summarize the 3 methods briefly.

outline.h2: Seismic Retrofit: When Earthquakes Are the Problem
h3: Cripple Wall Bracing and Foundation Bolting
outline.notes: Cripple wall bracing: adding plywood shear panels to short walls between foundation and first floor. Foundation bolting: attaching wood mudsill to concrete foundation with anchor bolts. Cost: $3K-$15K for typical single-family retrofit. Soft-story: multi-unit buildings with ground-floor garages/open space, mandatory under SF Mandatory Soft-Story Program. Cost $60K-$200K+.

outline.h2: The Earthquake Brace + Bolt Program
outline.notes: California Residential Mitigation Program (CRMP) offers $3,000 grants to eligible homeowners in specific ZIP codes for retrofit. Explain eligibility, application timing (usually January-February), typical process. Named grant program is highly citable content.

outline.h2: SF Mandatory Soft-Story Retrofit Program
outline.notes: SF passed mandatory ordinance in 2013 requiring wood-frame multi-unit buildings 3+ stories with soft first story (garage, open ground floor) to retrofit. Deadlines have passed for most tiers but enforcement continues. If you own a multi-unit building matching this description, this is not optional.

outline.h2: When You Need Both (Rare, But Real)
outline.notes: Marina fill homes, some Sunset homes on Colma sand, and older Mission Bay homes on bay mud may need underpinning AND seismic retrofit. Order matters: underpin first, retrofit second. Combined cost $30K-$100K+.

outline.h2: Comparison Table: Underpinning vs Seismic Retrofit
outline.notes: Table: Problem addressed, Typical cost, Timeline, Permit type, Grant availability, When you need it.

outline.h2: How to Get an Honest Diagnosis
outline.notes: What a proper foundation inspection includes: crawlspace access, laser level for floor slope, crack measurement, bolt-count on mudsill, cripple wall inspection, soil observation. Red flags in bids: quoting underpinning without measuring floor slope, quoting retrofit without counting existing bolts.

outline.h2: Ready to Diagnose Your Foundation?
outline.notes: CTA.
